disclaimer: Opportunistic measurements on a low-dose, non-contrast heart scan, for curiosity and education. Not a medical device and not a diagnosis; the official radiologist report is what counts.

confidenceLegend.measured: Read directly from the images with a defined method (or by the radiologist).
confidenceLegend.AI estimate: Depends on an AI outline that can't be fully checked on a scan without contrast dye.
confidenceLegend.rough: Ballpark only: the method or the scan type limits accuracy.

metrics.label: Whole heart
metrics.caption: Everything inside the heart's outline: four chambers plus walls. About 1.2 soda cans' worth.
metrics.context: Adult hearts are roughly fist-sized; volume depends on body size and on the moment in the heartbeat. This is a size description, not a test result.
metrics.method: TotalSegmentator v2 'heart' mask on the 1.5 mm thin series (0.74 x 0.74 x 0.75 mm voxels), voxel count x voxel volume. Image reconstructed at BestDiast 76% of the R-R interval (mid-diastole).

metrics.label: Blood in the four chambers
metrics.caption: How much blood each chamber held at the moment the picture was taken (heart relaxing, about three-quarters of the way through the beat).
metrics.context: Without contrast dye, blood and heart muscle look the same grey on CT, so the AI infers the inner walls from shape. Treat these as ballpark numbers; echo or MRI measure chambers properly, and their normal ranges don't transfer directly to this.
metrics.method: TotalSegmentator v1 cardiac model (LA, LV, RA, RV) on the thin series; voxel counts. Non-contrast, low-dose, ECG-triggered at BestDiast 76%.

metrics.label: Left-ventricle muscle mass
metrics.caption: The main pumping muscle: 96 mL of tissue, which weighs about 100 g (heart muscle is 1.05 g per mL).
metrics.context: Healthy adult men typically measure roughly 90-180 g on cardiac MRI (exact ranges vary by method and body size). A thick, heavy wall can follow years of high blood pressure.
metrics.method: TotalSegmentator v1 'heart_myocardium' (left-ventricular wall incl. septum) volume x 1.05 g/mL. On non-contrast CT the inner wall border is inferred by the AI, so the split between muscle and cavity is uncertain by perhaps +-20%.

metrics.label: Fat around the heart (epicardial)
metrics.caption: About 87 mL of fat sits inside the heart's sac, packed around the coronary arteries: roughly 6 tablespoons.
metrics.context: Studies of middle-aged adults typically find roughly 50-150 mL, rising with age and weight. More epicardial fat goes with more coronary plaque; there is no single agreed cut-off and definitions differ between studies.
metrics.method: Calcium-score series (3 mm slices every 1.5 mm, 0.31 mm pixels, soft Sa36d kernel): the reconstruction epicardial-fat studies use on calcium scans. Its noise is low (SD 20 HU in blood) and its 158 mm field of view contains the whole pericardium; the sharp thin series (SD 236 HU) would scatter muscle and air into the fat window. Fat = voxels from -190 to -30 HU inside the AI pericardium mask (TotalSegmentator trunk_cavities), excluding the heart's interior (chamber/heart masks eroded by 3 mm, so fat in the grooves on the heart's surface still counts). Subtracting the full heart masks instead gives 70 mL (they swallow some groove fat); counting every fat voxel in the sac gives 89 mL. Mean fat density -86 HU.

metrics.label: Liver density
metrics.caption: Fat makes the liver look darker on CT. A healthy liver is brighter than 40 HU.
metrics.context: Non-contrast CT: liver under 40 HU suggests at least moderate fatty liver; healthy livers usually sit around 50-70 HU.
metrics.method: Chest soft-tissue series (3 mm, Br40d kernel, 120 kV: the energy the published cut-offs assume). AI masks (TotalSegmentator) shrunk 5 mm in-plane and one slice up/down so no edge, rib or lung pixels leak in; mean HU of all remaining voxels. Only the top of the liver and spleen are inside this heart scan. Liver: 363,208 voxels (345 mL), SD 33 HU, median 64 HU.

metrics.label: Spleen density (reference)
metrics.caption: The spleen doesn't store fat, so it's the yardstick the liver is compared against.
metrics.method: Chest soft-tissue series (3 mm, Br40d kernel, 120 kV: the energy the published cut-offs assume). AI masks (TotalSegmentator) shrunk 5 mm in-plane and one slice up/down so no edge, rib or lung pixels leak in; mean HU of all remaining voxels. Only the top of the liver and spleen are inside this heart scan. Spleen: 29,855 voxels (28 mL), SD 34 HU.

metrics.label: Liver minus spleen
metrics.caption: Liver brighter than spleen: the healthy pattern.
metrics.context: Below -10 HU (liver much darker than spleen) suggests fatty liver; healthy livers usually read a few HU brighter than the spleen.
metrics.method: Chest soft-tissue series (3 mm, Br40d kernel, 120 kV: the energy the published cut-offs assume). AI masks (TotalSegmentator) shrunk 5 mm in-plane and one slice up/down so no edge, rib or lung pixels leak in; mean HU of all remaining voxels. Only the top of the liver and spleen are inside this heart scan.

metrics.label: Spine bone density
metrics.caption: Average inner-bone density of the fully scanned vertebrae (T7-T10): comfortably dense.
metrics.context: An opportunistic screen, not a DEXA scan. At the L1 vertebra, values above ~160 HU make osteoporosis unlikely and values under ~110 HU make it likely; mid-back vertebrae read about the same or a little higher than L1, so the comparison is approximate.
metrics.method: Vertebral bodies from TotalSegmentator's vertebrae_body task, split into levels with the v1 vertebra labels (v1's level boundaries matched the rib attachments for ribs 7-11; v2 mislabelled the top two bodies). Masks moved onto the chest soft-tissue series (3 mm, Br40d, 120 kV), shrunk 3 mm in-plane and one slice in z to drop the hard outer shell; mean HU of the spongy bone inside. Bodies cut by the edge of the scan are shown but not averaged.

metrics.label: Lung volume inside the scan
metrics.caption: Right 1.8 L + left 1.7 L of lung inside the 14 cm slab the scan covered. The scan targets the heart, so the lung tops are cut off.
metrics.context: The hospital's ClearRead CT software reported 1.9 L right and 1.8 L left: close to these AI numbers, and also limited to the scanned part. Whole lungs hold roughly 6 L in a deep breath, so this is not a lung-function test.
metrics.method: TotalSegmentator v2 lobe masks on the 1.5 mm thin series; voxel counts. Breath-hold inspiration, partial coverage (heart scan range only).

metrics.label: Emphysema index (LAA-950)
metrics.caption: Share of lung so dark (below -950 HU) that it could be emphysema, the air-trapping damage from smoking. Here it is mostly image noise.
metrics.context: Under about 5% is generally read as normal on standard-dose, smooth-kernel scans. This scan is low-dose and only covers part of the lungs, both of which push the number up. The same calculation on the sharp lung-kernel series gives a meaningless 37% because its noise (SD 145 HU in blood vs 22 HU on the smooth series) pushes normal lung below -950 HU.
metrics.method: Lung = the five AI lobe masks minus airways (dilated 1 voxel), shrunk 2 voxels in-plane (drops the dark undershoot rim the image filter leaves along the pleura; same approach as the AI second read); the scanner's blank padding slice at the top is skipped; percentage of voxels below -950 HU. Reported on the 3 mm smooth Br40d series (emphysema scoring calls for a smooth kernel); mean lung density -851 HU, 15th percentile -921 HU. Sharp Bl64d lung series for comparison: 37% (15th percentile clipped at -1024 HU).

metrics.label: Ascending aorta
metrics.caption: The main artery leaving the heart, measured across by the radiologist.
metrics.context: In adult men the ascending aorta is usually under about 40 mm (it grows slowly with age and body size); radiologists start calling it dilated from around 40-45 mm.
metrics.method: Radiologist's caliper on the chest soft-tissue series (instance 13), recovered from the DICOM presentation state. AI cross-check on the same slice: area-equivalent diameter 36.5 mm (narrowest-widest 36.6-39.8 mm).

metrics.label: Main pulmonary artery
metrics.caption: The artery carrying blood from the heart to the lungs, measured just before it splits in two. A wide one can be a sign of high blood pressure in the lungs.
metrics.context: Framingham Heart Study (non-contrast heart CT, like this one): normal upper limit 29 mm in men (27 mm in women).
metrics.method: Double-oblique reformat of the calcium-score series (soft kernel, 0.31 mm pixels). Vessel axis fitted through the centres of perpendicular cross-sections of the AI pulmonary-artery mask (tilted 23 degrees upward); bifurcation detected where the section stops being round. On 4 planes 2-8 mm before the split: AI-outline equivalent diameter 25.4-25.8 mm and edge-to-edge profile diameters (median per plane) 28.0-28.9 mm; final value = their average (26.7-27.2 mm across planes). Outer-wall diameter, as in the Framingham study (the wall can't be told apart from blood without contrast).

metrics.label: Pulmonary artery : aorta ratio
metrics.caption: The pulmonary artery should be narrower than the aorta beside it.
metrics.context: Framingham: ratios under 0.9 are normal; above 1.0 suggests raised lung blood pressure.
metrics.method: Main pulmonary artery (27.0 mm, above) divided by the radiologist's ascending aorta (36.1 mm) at the same level.

metrics.label: Scanner dose report (DLP)
metrics.caption: The scanner's own tally of radiation delivered along the scanned length.
metrics.context: CTDIvol 2.12 mGy, size-specific dose 2.87 mGy for a 27.4 cm-wide body. A typical full chest CT is several times higher.
metrics.method: Siemens dose report (DICOM structured report): Prospectively ECG-triggered sequential (step-and-shoot), 4 steps, 120 kV, 0.25 s rotation.

metrics.label: Effective dose
metrics.caption: About 52 days of the natural radiation everyone absorbs anyway.
metrics.context: Effective dose converts the scan into whole-body risk terms. The everyday comparisons use rounded reference values.
metrics.method: DLP 31.39 mGy·cm x k = 0.014 mSv/(mGy·cm), the standard adult chest conversion factor. Some cardiac-imaging groups use a heart-specific k = 0.026, which would give 0.8 mSv; still a low dose.
